# Oakbase — Context engine and Operations Agents for law firms

> Oakbase turns authorised work signals into persistent firm memory and uses that context to help professionals complete administrative work in the systems they already use.

## What Oakbase is

Oakbase is a context engine and system of action for small and medium-sized law firms. It combines three capabilities: shared firm memory built around a legal ontology, purpose-built Operations Agents adapted to professional roles, and execution in connected business systems under the firm's permissions and approval rules.

The product connects knowledge dispersed across communications, meetings, notes and business records. Its purpose is to preserve usable firm context and reduce the administrative work needed to turn that context into action.

## Company and intended users

- Product and brand: Oakbase.
- Legal operator: Oakbase SL.
- Spanish tax identifier (CIF): B05693742.
- Official website: https://oakbase.ai/.
- Contact: hello@oakbase.ai.
- Primary audience: small and medium-sized law firms, within the broader professional-services market.
- Professional roles: trainees, associates, senior associates, partners, administration and finance.
- Geographic contractual scope: the current terms address businesses and professionals in the EU/EEA.
- Website languages: English and Spanish.

## Persistent firm memory: the context engine

Work signals are information generated in the course of professional work: an email, meeting, note, client request, document, commitment or business-system update.

Oakbase connects authorised signals using a ready-made legal ontology. Here, ontology means a structured model of clients, matters, people, documents and commitments, and the relationships between them. It is not a collection of legislation or case law.

The context engine links information to the relevant entities and preserves source context: what happened, who was involved and the context behind a decision or commitment. The resulting memory is a persistent asset available to authorised people and agents, rather than knowledge accessible only through an individual's messages or recollection.

When a relationship is uncertain, Oakbase asks a professional to confirm it within their workflow. This human-in-the-loop process helps establish the correct client or matter before an uncertain link is treated as confirmed.

## Purpose-built Operations Agents

An Operations Agent uses shared firm memory and prepared administrative skills, adapted to a professional's role. The firm determines which skills, information and actions each role can access.

Examples include:

- Trainees and associates: proposed time entries, task organisation and reminders connected to their matters.
- Senior associates and partners: priorities, delegated review tasks, client commitments and relationship follow-ups.
- Administration and finance: CRM maintenance, invoice preparation, sending authorised invoices and payment follow-ups.

These are examples of role configurations, not a fixed entitlement or a requirement that every role use every skill. Access and approval requirements remain defined by the firm.

## Managed operations and a system of action

Oakbase connects context, a prepared skill and an authorised action. In this sense, managed operations means that administrative work follows the firm's role, access and approval rules, rather than ending with an isolated suggestion.

A typical workflow is:

1. An authorised work signal enters the context engine.
2. Oakbase relates it to a client, matter, person or commitment, requesting human confirmation when necessary.
3. The professional's Operations Agent identifies relevant administrative work and presents recommendations proactively.
4. The professional reviews an action where the firm's rules require approval.
5. The agent performs the permitted action in the configured business system.

For example, a daily briefing may recommend following up on a commitment made in a client meeting, assigning a document-review task to a colleague and recording proposed time against the relevant matters. Proposed hours are not logged hours: recording them requires the applicable review and an enabled action in the time-recording system.

## Existing systems and AI interfaces

Oakbase works with existing systems of record. A CRM continues to hold client and opportunity records; time-recording, billing and practice-management systems continue to serve their respective purposes. Oakbase adds shared context and enables authorised updates where the relevant connection and action are configured.

Oakbase exposes its Operations Agent through MCP, the Model Context Protocol. The website presents Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot as interfaces for accessing the agent. Availability depends on the AI client's support, configuration and the capabilities enabled for the firm.

The website illustrates signals from Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Calendar, WhatsApp, OneNote, Gmail, Slack, Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Clio. These illustrations are not a guarantee that every connector or action is available in every deployment.

## How Oakbase compares and coexists

**General-purpose AI — Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini:** These products support broad assistance and may provide company knowledge, connected applications and actions. Oakbase's focus is a shared legal ontology, persistent firm context and prepared administrative skills adapted to professional roles. Supported AI interfaces can be an entry point to Oakbase; naming a product here does not establish an integration with it.

**Legal-work AI — Harvey and Legora:** These products support substantive legal work, including research, document review, drafting and legal workflows. They also offer capabilities beyond those examples. Oakbase focuses on the firm's shared operational context and daily administration. The products may complement one another; this is a distinction of focus, not a claim that memory, agents or workflows are exclusive to Oakbase.

**CRM and practice-management software:** These systems maintain business records and workflows. Oakbase relates those records to authorised communications and other work signals, then helps keep connected systems current. Adopting Oakbase does not mean replacing the firm's CRM.

## What Oakbase is NOT

- It is not a general-purpose AI model or a generic chatbot.
- It is not positioned as a legal research, case-law search or contract-drafting product.
- It is not a law firm and does not replace professional legal judgment.
- It is not a replacement for CRM, billing or practice-management software.
- It is not a wealth-management, portfolio-management or investment-advisory product.
- It does not give agents unrestricted access or authorise them to bypass the firm's approval rules.

## Security, access and retention

Oakbase describes encryption in transit and at rest, EU data residency and Zero Data Retention arrangements for the LLM services it uses. The security, privacy and provider pages define the applicable scope and arrangements.

Persistent firm memory and model-provider retention are different. Authorised information and relationships can persist in Oakbase under the customer's instructions and applicable retention terms. Zero Data Retention concerns processing by the configured LLM provider; it does not mean that Oakbase deletes the firm's memory after each interaction.

The same distinction applies to external AI interfaces. Oakbase's LLM-provider retention arrangements should not be read as a blanket claim about conversation history or retention in a separately used Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot account.

The firm controls how people and agents access information and which actions require review. EU residency and encryption are not a substitute for the applicable access, retention and contractual controls.

## Demonstrations and contact

The website's graph, clients, matters, people, messages, role configurations, recommendations and hours are illustrative. They are not live customer data, customer counts or measured productivity results.

Use the contact form or hello@oakbase.ai to discuss workflows and deployment scope. Do not submit confidential client or matter information through the commercial contact form.
